conceptZh: 菜：草字頭加「采」，採來吃的青菜；披風英雄和一棵愛模仿的小青菜一起把葉子排成字。
object: a caped action-figure hero with a far-too-long crimson cape, and a tiny bok choy sprout with a face that copies him
morph: hero and the mimicking sprout swing leafy blades one beat apart until the blades land as the top grass radical and the lower strokes of 菜
creativeAngle: 披風英雄的披風長三號，老是蓋住自己的頭；一棵小青菜學他每個動作，慢一拍，結果兩邊揮出的葉片剛好落成字的筆畫。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale butter-yellow backdrop, no props beyond those named. Cast: a chunky caped action-figure hero with a crimson cape three sizes too long that keeps flopping over his own head, plus one tiny bok choy sprout with a round face that mimics him one beat late. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 菜, drawn in saturated leaf-green strokes with a slightly darker edge, finishing centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the hero slides in on one foot and strikes a grand sword-swing pose holding a long leaf blade; the cape flops over his face and he peeks out. The first narrated 菜 lands as the blade swishes and leaves a green horizontal stroke hanging in the air. 1.5-3.5s: the bok choy sprout pops up from a little clay pot at his feet and copies the swing a beat late, whacking the hero's boot; both blades flick and the two top strokes of the grass radical settle together. The second narrated 菜 lands exactly as the radical clicks in. 3.5-5.0s: the hero spins to shake off the cape, the sprout spins too, one beat behind, and tangles itself in the cape's tail; their wobbly swings throw green leaf strokes down in a neat row and the lower part of the glyph fills in. As the word is spoken the sprout hops into a small wooden crate and a fresh pile of glossy green vegetables pops up beside it. 5.0-8.0s: the finished glyph is perfectly still and fully readable for the last 3 seconds while the hero, off to one side, tries a proud pose, the cape flops over his head again, and the sprout copies with a tiny bow. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 菜、菜、青菜 (ㄘㄞˋ、ㄘㄞˋ、ㄑㄧㄥ ㄘㄞˋ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles, labels, watermarks or flashing effects; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon creatures, with no real people.
